content:
After a long developer and public beta period, Apple is now rolling out macOS 26.6 to all users with compatible Macs. Here is what's included in this update.

macOS 26.6 Officially Released

macOS 26.6 has officially launched, fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities, along with other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include an issue that incorrectly displayed deactivation notices for some Intel-only apps, as well as bugs affecting HDR screenshots in HealthKit and Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 is believed to begin an indexing process to support the new Siri AI, the Siri app, and other features related to the new Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed this process for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but Mac users seem to be getting the same arrangement. As users currently testing the macOS 27 beta know, the indexing process takes several days, so starting it now should shorten the wait time after upgrading later.

The official build number for macOS 26.6 is 25G72, which differs from last week's RC version (25G70).

Have you discovered anything new in macOS 26.6? Let us know in the comments.
